s:

b. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights

s:
Consider the following statements:

1. The NCSC is provided for under Article 338.
2. The NCST is provided for under Article 338A.
3. The NCBC is provided for under Article 338B.
4. The National Commission for Women is provided for under Article 338C.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The NCW is a statutory body under the NCW Act, 1990 and is not established under Article 338C.
tq: Check the constitutional Article attached to each commission and reject the invented Article.
sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

s:
Which of the following statements regarding commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes is correct?

a. The 65th Constitutional Amendment of 1990 created separate commissions for the SCs and STs.
b. The 89th Constitutional Amendment of 2003 bifurcated the combined commission into the NCSC and NCST.
c. The separate commissions began functioning in 1990.
d. The NCST is established under Article 338B.
o: The 65th Constitutional Amendment of 1990 created separate commissions for the SCs and STs.
The separate commissions began functioning in 1990.
The NCST is established under Article 338B.
The 89th Constitutional Amendment of 2003 bifurcated the combined commission into the NCSC and NCST.
x: The 65th Amendment created a combined SC/ST Commission. The 89th Amendment in 2003 bifurcated it, and separate bodies functioned from 2004; the NCST is under Article 338A.
tq: Watch for swapped amendment numbers, Articles and dates in constitutional-body questions.
sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

s:
Which one of the following is NOT a statutory body under the Ministry of Women and Child Development?

a. National Commission for Women
b. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
c. Central Adoption Resource Authority
d. National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
x: NCW, NCPCR and CARA are the three statutory bodies under the Ministry of Women and Child Development. The NCSK is under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and is non-statutory since 2004.
tq: Find the body belonging to the neighbouring ministry and different legal category.
sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

s:
Which one of the following statements regarding linguistic minorities is correct?

a. Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the National Commission for Minorities under the NCM Act, 1992.
b. Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
c. Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the NCBC under Article 338B.
d. Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the National Commission for Women.
o: Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the National Commission for Women.
Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the National Commission for Minorities under the NCM Act, 1992.
Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the NCBC under Article 338B.
x: Linguistic minorities do not fall under the National Commission for Minorities. They fall under the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities provided under Article 350B.
tq: Separate religious-minority institutions from the constitutional protection for linguistic minorities.
sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

s:
The National Commission for Women consists of:

a. A Chairperson, three Members and a Member-Secretary
b. A Chairperson, five Members and a Member-Secretary
c. A Chairperson, seven Members and a Secretary-General
d. Five Members and a Secretary appointed by Parliament
o: A Chairperson, seven Members and a Secretary-General
A Chairperson, three Members and a Member-Secretary
Five Members and a Secretary appointed by Parliament
A Chairperson, five Members and a Member-Secretary
x: The NCW comprises one Chairperson, five Members and one Member-Secretary. All are nominated by the Central Government.
tq: Use the exact composition and do not confuse nomination with election or parliamentary appointment.

Who nominates the Chairperson, Members and Member-Secretary of the National Commission for Women?

a. The President of India
b. The Parliament
c. The Central Government
d. The Supreme Court of India
x: The Chairperson, five Members and Member-Secretary of the NCW are nominated by the Central Government.
tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” method to distinguish nomination from constitutional appointment.

s:
Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Women?

a. Jayanti Patnaik
b. Vijaya Rahatkar
c. Mohini Giri
d. Girija Vyas
x: Jayanti Patnaik was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Women.

s:
Which one of the following is NOT a function of the National Commission for Women?

a. Suggesting amendments to laws affecting women
b. Taking suo motu notice where women’s rights are denied
c. Commissioning special studies on discrimination and atrocities against women
d. Enforcing criminal sentences imposed by courts
o: Suggesting amendments to laws affecting women
Taking suo motu notice where women’s rights are denied
Commissioning special studies on discrimination and atrocities against women
Enforcing criminal sentences imposed by courts
x: The NCW may review laws, suggest amendments, take suo motu notice and commission special studies. It does not enforce criminal sentences imposed by courts.
tq: Reject the option that converts a recommendatory statutory function into a coercive judicial power.
sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Women:

1. The Central Government must consult it on all major policy matters affecting women.
2. It may appoint committees for particular purposes.
3. It may co-opt persons from outside the Commission.
4. It has no power to regulate its own procedure.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The NCW may regulate its own procedure, so statement 4 is false.
tq: Spot the negative statement that reverses an expressly stated procedural power.
sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

s:
In the context of women’s rights, a ‘Jan Sunwai’ refers to:

a. A closed-door meeting of judges
b. A public hearing of women’s grievances
c. An annual financial audit of women’s commissions
d. A legislative session on gender budgeting
o: A public hearing of women’s grievances
A legislative session on gender budgeting
An annual financial audit of women’s commissions
x: Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings conducted to hear and address women’s grievances.
tq: Test the exact meaning of a programme term rather than its broad policy context.
sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

b. Periodic tenure extensions by government resolution

d. Orders of the Supreme Court alone
o: Orders of the Supreme Court alone
Periodic tenure extensions by government resolution
Annual elections conducted by sanitation workers
x: After the NCSK Act lapsed in 2004, the Commission continued as a non-statutory body through periodic tenure extensions by government resolution.
tq: Apply the legal-status distinction to determine the present institutional basis.
sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

s:
In January 2022, the Union Cabinet extended the tenure of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis for:

b. Two years beyond 31 March 2022

b. Conducting the census of all urban households
c. Appointing municipal commissioners in every State
d. Issuing constitutional amendments concerning sanitation

Conducting the census of all urban households
Monitoring the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 and reporting to the Government
x: The NCSK monitors implementation of the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 and reports to the Government.

Consider the following statements regarding the Paris Principles:
1. They were adopted in Paris in October 1991.
2. They were endorsed by the United Nations General Assembly on 20 December 1993.
3. They exclusively concern the protection of linguistic minorities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

o: Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes
Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes
Chairperson of the National Commission for Women
Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities

o: Six years or until attaining 70 years, whichever is earlier
Five years or until attaining 65 years, whichever is earlier
Three years or until attaining 70 years, whichever is earlier, with reappointment allowed

s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Adoption of the Paris Principles
B. Promulgation of the Ordinance preceding the PHRA
C. Establishment of the NHRC
D. Endorsement of the Paris Principles by the UN General Assembly
x: The Paris Principles were adopted in October 1991, the Ordinance was promulgated on 28 September 1993, the NHRC was established on 12 October 1993, and UNGA endorsement followed on 20 December 1993.

sec: NHRC - PHRA 1993, composition, chairperson eligibility, appointment committee  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is a power exercised by the NHRC while conducting an inquiry?
o: Power to amend the law under which the inquiry is conducted
Power to impose a binding monetary penalty on the Union Government
Powers of a civil court for summoning witnesses and calling for documents
Power to punish every witness for contempt without judicial process
x: During inquiries, the NHRC has the powers of a civil court, including summoning witnesses, calling for documents and receiving evidence on affidavit. It cannot itself amend legislation or impose a binding monetary penalty on the government.
tq: Ask which authority has the procedural power rather than the final coercive power.
sec: Human Rights Commissions - functions, limits, time bar, binding or not, SHRC appointment  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements about the recommendations of the NHRC:
1. They are binding on the government.
2. The government is required to respond to them.
3. The Commission cannot compel implementation of its recommendations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: NHRC recommendations are not binding. However, the government must respond, and the Commission cannot compel their implementation.
tq: Separate the duty to respond from the power to compel implementation.
sec: Human Rights Commissions - functions, limits, time bar, binding or not, SHRC appointment  [APPSC]

s: A complaint alleging a human-rights violation committed eighteen months ago is ordinarily outside the jurisdiction of the NHRC because the Commission
o: cannot inquire into an incident after one year from its occurrence
has jurisdiction only over incidents occurring outside India
can inquire only after a criminal conviction
can inquire only into incidents committed by private persons
x: The NHRC cannot inquire into a complaint after one year from the date of the alleged violation.
tq: Apply the statutory time-bar rule to a factual situation.
sec: Human Rights Commissions - functions, limits, time bar, binding or not, SHRC appointment  [APPSC]

s: In relation to alleged human-rights violations by members of the armed forces, the NHRC may primarily
o: transfer the case to a State Human Rights Commission
issue a binding order to the commanding officer
seek a report from the Central Government
x: The NHRC’s role concerning the armed forces is limited; it may seek a report from the Central Government and act within the statutory framework.
tq: Use the limited-power trap where a reporting power is mistaken for direct enforcement.
sec: Human Rights Commissions - functions, limits, time bar, binding or not, SHRC appointment

State List and Concurrent List subjects

s: A State Human Rights Commission shall not ordinarily take up a matter that is already before

s:
Consider the following statements about international human-rights documents:
1. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in 1948.
2. The ICCPR and ICESCR were adopted in 1966.
3. CEDAW was adopted in 1979.
4. The Convention against Torture was adopted in 1984.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct: the UDHR dates to 1948, the ICCPR and ICESCR to 1966, CEDAW to 1979 and the Convention against Torture to 1984.
tq: Arrange a compact list of dates without allowing one familiar year to distort the others.

tq: Link the commemorative date to the correct international instrument.

s: Under Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, the expression “minority” refers to:
o: Any community notified by the President
Any community notified by the Central Government
Any community recognised by the Supreme Court
Any community notified by the concerned State Government
x: Section 2(c) does not define minority independently; it refers to any community notified by the Central Government.
tq: Test the exact statutory authority instead of assuming that the President or State Government issues the notification.
sec: National Commission for Minorities - notified communities, recent additions

s: Which one of the following communities was NOT among those notified as minority communities in 1993?
x: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis were notified in 1993. Jains were added later, on 27 January 2014.
tq: Use the chronological distinction between the original notified communities and the later addition.
sec: National Commission for Minorities - notified communities, recent additions

s: Jains were notified as a minority community in India on:
x: Jains were added to the list of notified minority communities on 27 January 2014.
tq: Distinguish the close year options by anchoring the later addition to its exact date.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the notified minority communities in India:
1. Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis were notified in 1993.
2. Jains were added to the notified list in 2014.
3. There are six notified minority communities after the addition of Jains.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The five communities notified in 1993 became six after Jains were added in 2014.
tq: Check the original list, the later addition and the resulting total separately.

s: The National Commission for Minorities consists of:
o: A Chairperson and five members appointed by the President
A Chairperson, two Vice-Chairpersons and four members
A Chairperson and six members, without a Vice-Chairperson
A Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five members
x: The Commission has seven members: a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five members. The Vice-Chairperson was added by the 1995 amendment.
tq: Test composition and the amendment-created office together, while using the President as the authority trap.
sec: National Commission for Minorities - notified communities, recent additions

1. The Commission consists of seven members.
2. At least five members, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities.
3. The Vice-Chairperson was included through the 1995 amendment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Commission has seven members, at least five including the Chairperson must belong to minority communities, and the Vice-Chairperson was added by the 1995 amendment.
tq: Verify the numerical composition, community representation and amendment detail independently.

s: Which of the following correctly explains the relevance of Articles 338(9) and 338A(10)?

They empower the President to appoint all State commission members.
They transfer the reports of State commissions to Parliament.
They require the Union and States to consult the concerned National Commission on policy matters affecting the communities concerned.
x: Articles 338(9) and 338A(10) concern consultation with the National Commissions on major policy matters; they do not create State commissions.
tq: Reject the wrong institutional function by distinguishing consultation clauses from establishment provisions.

Consider the following statements regarding State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights:
1. They function under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005.
2. They exist as State counterparts alongside the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights.
3. They oversee child-rights directions such as those relating to menstrual hygiene in schools.

With reference to the National Commissions for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Backward Classes, consider the following statements:
1. They have the powers of a civil court while investigating or inquiring into matters.
2. They may summon and enforce the attendance of persons and examine them on oath.
3. They may requisition public records from any office or organization.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The NCSC, NCST and NCBC exercise civil-court powers during investigations and inquiries, including summoning persons, examining them on oath, calling for documents and requisitioning public records.
tq: Combine several related powers and verify each statement rather than relying on one familiar power.
sec: Powers of commissions - civil court powers, investigation, reports to whom (NCSC, NCST, NCBC)

s: The civil-court powers of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, while investigating or inquiring into matters, are derived from which Article of the Constitution?
x: Article 338 provides the constitutional basis for the powers of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes. Article 338A relates to the NCST and Article 338B to the NCBC.
tq: Use the article-number distinction among closely related constitutional commissions.
sec: Powers of commissions - civil court powers, investigation, reports to whom (NCSC, NCST, NCBC)

s: Article 338B of the Constitution deals with the National Commission for:
x: Article 338B provides for the National Commission for Backward Classes. The NCST is dealt with under Article 338A.
tq: Test the exact constitutional article through a closely confusable commission name.

tq: Apply the ‘who receives the report?’ method to distinguish the reporting authority from the laying authority.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the reports of the NCSC, NCST and NCBC:
1. The President lays the reports before Parliament.
2. An action-taken memorandum accompanies the reports.
3. Portions concerning a particular State are sent to the Governor of that State.
4. The Union and every State are required to consult these commissions on major policy matters affecting their subjects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct. The reports are submitted to the President, laid before Parliament with an action-taken memorandum, and State-related portions go to the concerned Governor; major policy matters require consultation with the commissions.
tq: Separate submission, laying, State transmission and consultation duties instead of treating them as one procedure.

s:
With reference to the powers of statutory commissions in inquiries, consider the following statements:
1. The NHRC has civil-court powers.
2. The National Commission for Minorities has powers under its Act that enable it to exercise civil-court powers in inquiries.
3. The National Commission for Minorities has no automatic civil-court powers independent of its statutory framework.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The NHRC has civil-court powers in inquiries, while the NCM’s inquiry powers arise from its statutory framework and should not be described as automatic or unrestricted constitutional powers.
tq: Distinguish statutory powers from automatic or constitutional powers when similar commissions are compared.

Which of the following developments was associated with criticism concerning the National Commission for Minorities and the NHRC in 2026?
1. The post of NCM Chairperson remained vacant for 15 months.
2. An adviser resigned from the NHRC LGBTQI+ core group over the Transgender Persons Amendment Bill, 2026.
3. The NHRC was dissolved following the resignation.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. A long vacancy affected the NCM, and an adviser resigned from the NHRC LGBTQI+ core group over the Transgender Persons Amendment Bill, 2026; the NHRC was not dissolved.
tq: Find the false institutional consequence in a set containing two current-affairs facts and one exaggerated claim.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the constitutional status of the commissions listed below?
o: All commissions listed are constitutional bodies with identical powers
NCSC, NCST and NCBC are constitutional bodies; the other commissions depend on parliamentary Acts
NHRC, NCM and NCW are constitutional bodies; NCSC is statutory
Only NHRC and NCM are constitutional bodies
x: The NCSC, NCST and NCBC are constitutional commissions. Bodies such as the NHRC, NCM and NCW derive their existence from parliamentary Acts, which Parliament may amend or allow to lapse.
tq: Separate constitutional bodies from statutory bodies before comparing their legal status.

Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Jains notified as a national minority
B. Harjit Singh Grewal became Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities
C. National Commission for Scheduled Castes began a full review of de-reservation proposals
